expected.charges: Possession of unregistered destructive devices (Molotov cocktails)

operations.name: Toshitaka Robert Kitajima

expected.name: Toshitaka Robert Kitajima
expected.description: Toshitaka Robert Kitajima was a Nisei Japanese American from Kohala, Hawaii Island, and a son of Yoshio and Roku Kitajima. JCCH records his birth year as 1931. His own individual record documents December 1942 mainland transfer aboard Lurline, Jerome confinement January 1943-May 1944, Tule Lake confinement May 1944-November 1945 and December 1945 return to Honolulu aboard Shawnee. His family confinement timeline is distinct from the December 1941 arrest of his father. This was administrative US wartime confinement in the context of Japanese ancestry; the archive establishes no individual criminal conviction. Source: https://incarceration.jcchawaii.org/internees/kitajima-toshitaka-robert

operations.source: Individual funeral-home obituary: https://www.fukuimortuary.com/obituaries/robert-kitajima . Robert Toshitaka Kitajima, Hawaii-born Nisei and former Tule Lake internee, born June 2, 1931 and died March 12, 2009. Full name, Hawaii origin, birth year and Tule Lake custody match JCCH profile. Adds only missing death date; existing year-only birth and photograph preserved.

operations.name: Alexander Scott

expected.name: Alexander Scott
expected.description: Alexander Scott was the editor of the Passaic Weekly Issue, a socialist newspaper that covered the 1913 Paterson silk strike sympathetically. He was prosecuted under New Jersey's 1902 Criminal Anarchy Law — passed after the McKinley assassination — for editorials condemning Paterson police violence against strikers. Sentenced to 1 to 15 years at the New Jersey State Prison in Trenton, his case became a landmark First Amendment fight for the early labor and free-speech movements.

operations.source: Contemporary International Socialist Review, July 1913 p10, caption COMRADE SCOTT, article The Conviction of Alexander Scott. Reproduced with explicit identification at https://weneverforget.org/hellraisers-journal-international-socialist-review-the-conviction-of-alexander-scott-editor-of-the-weekly-issue-of-passaic-county/ .
